beats.why: Officials say it saves drinking water and groundwater as rain stays weak.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Update, Nov 2: It's live. HMWSSB managing director K. Ashok Reddy launched the green water tanker programme at the Telangana Secretariat on Sunday, the board's 37th Foundation Day (The Hindu). Treated wastewater from registered sewage treatment plants (STPs) goes out in branded green tankers marked 'Strictly for non-domestic use and not for drinking'. Phase 1: 19 STPs and 28 tankers. Government departments, public parks and greenery needs get priority first. About 100 tankers from GHMC, HMDA and private firms have registered to join. Coming soon: a booking system, GPS tracking and e-POS. Prices: not announced yet. The Secretariat itself uses 250 kilolitres of drinking water a day, 50 of it for non-drinking needs; a pipeline from a 20 MLD STP will now cover that. Officials say the scheme follows a directive from CM A. Revanth Reddy. Earlier (Oct 17): the board wants 500 million litres a day of treated water used for non-drinking needs.
Borewells that once struck water at 300 feet are failing far deeper, Telangana Today reports.

cards.body: Hyderabad supplies about 150 litres per person a day, more than Bengaluru (108) or Chennai (135), yet still falls short of demand.

cards.q: Why is Hyderabad pushing treated water for builders?
cards.why: With weak rain and a supply gap, using treated water for construction leaves more clean water for homes.
